title: Build or Burn
endLine: The malonyl CoA that builds fat also shuts the gate to burning.

scenes.tts: A fed cell builds palmitate two carbons at a time. Each turn costs one A T P and two N A D P H. But the same cell also holds mitochondria that burn fat. So what stops new fat from being burned as fast as it is made?
scenes.caption: A fed cell builds palmitate two carbons at a time. Each turn costs one ATP and two NADPH. But the same cell also holds mitochondria that burn fat. So what stops new fat from being burned as fast as it is made?
scenes.narration: A fed cell builds palmitate two carbons at a time. Each turn costs one ATP and two NADPH. But the same cell also holds mitochondria that burn fat. So what stops new fat from being burned as fast as it is made?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's dark schematic cytoplasm and its objects without a reset, now widened into one world kept all film. LEFT 55% of the frame: the first film's assembly floor, with the ACC gate, the ATP coin slot, rectangular malonyl extender blocks carrying their yellow carboxyl badge, the circular CRDR loop of fatty acid synthase, and green NADPH batteries at its two R stations. RIGHT 45%: one large rounded mitochondrion, drawn as a plain outline with a slow inner swirl, and a single door in its outer wall facing the floor (no label yet). A small 'schematic' tag sits at bottom right throughout. During the first two sentences, one malonyl block enters the loop, an ATP coin drops, two NADPH batteries drain and the chain counter ticks up by two. On 'mitochondria that burn fat', the mitochondrion's swirl brightens. On the question, a finished bar stamped 'palmitate' rolls off the loop and drifts toward the open door. Large text above: 'What keeps new fat unburned?'

Title 'Build or Burn' in two large words over the same world for 2 seconds while the question text fades out. The palmitate bar hovers halfway between the loop and the open door; belts and the mitochondrion's swirl keep moving.

scenes.tts: If both ran at once, the cell would build a chain, then tear it down, paying for both. Its separate places, carriers and electron pools make it possible to control each direction on its own. Building has one main control point.
scenes.caption: If both ran at once, the cell would build a chain, then tear it down, paying for both. Its separate places, carriers and electron pools make it possible to control each direction on its own. Building has one main control point.
scenes.narration: If both ran at once, the cell would build a chain, then tear it down, paying for both. Its separate places, carriers and electron pools make it possible to control each direction on its own. Building has one main control point.
scenes.visual: On 'build a chain, then tear it down', the palmitate bar slips through the open door; inside the mitochondrion it is chopped into two-carbon pieces that flicker out, while the loop builds another bar. A cost meter between them labelled 'paid twice' ticks down with each cycle (schematic). On 'separate places', a faint boundary line brightens between the cytoplasm floor and the mitochondrion. On 'one main control point', everything dims except the ACC gate on the left, which glows.

scenes.tts: That point is A C C, the enzyme that makes malonyl C O A. Citrate, which piles up when fuel is plentiful, switches it on. So does insulin. Palmitoyl C O A, the finished product, switches it off, a clean feedback brake.
scenes.caption: That point is ACC, the enzyme that makes malonyl CoA. Citrate, which piles up when fuel is plentiful, switches it on. So does insulin. Palmitoyl CoA, the finished product, switches it off, a clean feedback brake.
scenes.narration: That point is ACC, the enzyme that makes malonyl CoA. Citrate, which piles up when fuel is plentiful, switches it on. So does insulin. Palmitoyl CoA, the finished product, switches it off, a clean feedback brake.
scenes.visual: Camera eases toward the ACC gate so it fills about 60% of the frame height; the mitochondrion stays visible at the right edge. A large lever on the gate reads ON at top and OFF at bottom. On 'Citrate', small plain tokens labelled 'citrate' stream in and push the lever up; the gate's crank turns faster and malonyl blocks roll out. On 'insulin', a signal arrow labelled 'insulin signal' reaches in from the frame edge (the hormone stays outside the cell) and pushes it further up. On 'Palmitoyl CoA', a palmitate bar from the loop curls back as a token labelled 'palmitoyl CoA' and presses the lever down; the crank slows. Lever position is schematic, no numbers.

scenes.tts: A M P K, the cell's low-fuel sensor, also switches A C C off, by attaching a phosphate. Another enzyme, P P two A, removes the phosphate and turns it back on.
scenes.caption: AMPK, the cell's low-fuel sensor, also switches ACC off, by attaching a phosphate. Another enzyme, PP2A, removes the phosphate and turns it back on.
scenes.narration: AMPK, the cell's low-fuel sensor, also switches ACC off, by attaching a phosphate. Another enzyme, PP2A, removes the phosphate and turns it back on.
scenes.visual: Same gate and lever. A token labelled 'AMPK' clips a round tag marked 'P' onto the gate; the lever drops to OFF and the crank stops, with no malonyl blocks leaving. Then a token labelled 'PP2A' unclips the 'P' tag and carries it away; the lever rises and the crank turns again. At most five tokens on screen; the citrate and insulin tokens fade back to small icons at the gate's side.

scenes.tts: Now the elegant part. Malonyl C O A has a second job. It blocks C P T one, the gate fat must pass to enter the mitochondrion and be burned. So the molecule that commits a cell to building also shuts the door on burning.
scenes.caption: Now the elegant part. Malonyl CoA has a second job. It blocks CPT-I, the gate fat must pass to enter the mitochondrion and be burned. So the molecule that commits a cell to building also shuts the door on burning.
scenes.narration: Now the elegant part. Malonyl CoA has a second job. It blocks CPT-I, the gate fat must pass to enter the mitochondrion and be burned. So the molecule that commits a cell to building also shuts the door on burning.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the full world. Malonyl blocks leaving the ACC gate split: most roll into the CRDR loop, and one rolls right toward the mitochondrion. The door in its wall now gains the label 'CPT-I gate'. On 'blocks', the malonyl block wedges into the door and the door swings shut; a palmitate bar drifting toward it bumps the closed door and floats back. The mitochondrion's swirl dims. On the final sentence, two arrows from the same malonyl block light at once: one into the loop labelled 'build', one onto the door labelled 'block burning'.

scenes.tts: A C C comes in two forms. A C C one works in the cytoplasm and feeds the synthase. A C C two sits on the mitochondrion itself. Why put a fat-building enzyme on the organelle that burns fat?
scenes.caption: ACC comes in two forms. ACC1 works in the cytoplasm and feeds the synthase. ACC2 sits on the mitochondrion itself. Why put a fat-building enzyme on the organelle that burns fat?
scenes.narration: ACC comes in two forms. ACC1 works in the cytoplasm and feeds the synthase. ACC2 sits on the mitochondrion itself. Why put a fat-building enzyme on the organelle that burns fat?
scenes.visual: The single ACC gate splits into two copies of the same gate design. 'ACC1' slides to its old place on the floor beside the CRDR loop and keeps sending malonyl blocks into it. 'ACC2' slides right and settles on the mitochondrion's outer wall, a short distance from the closed CPT-I door; its crank turns slowly and nothing yet leaves it. Question text above: 'Why ACC2 on the mitochondrion?'

Deliberate thinking pause. Hold the question 'Why ACC2 on the mitochondrion?'. Both gates' cranks turn slowly, the CRDR loop keeps circling, and the mitochondrion's swirl moves faintly behind the closed door. Reveal nothing new.

scenes.tts: Because that is where the blocker is made. Much of the malonyl C O A that blocks C P T one comes from A C C two. A C C one's malonyl C O A is mainly a building block. A C C two's is mainly a signal.
scenes.caption: Because that is where the blocker is made. Much of the malonyl CoA that blocks CPT-I comes from ACC2. ACC1's malonyl CoA is mainly a building block. ACC2's is mainly a signal.
scenes.narration: Because that is where the blocker is made. Much of the malonyl CoA that blocks CPT-I comes from ACC2. ACC1's malonyl CoA is mainly a building block. ACC2's is mainly a signal.
scenes.visual: The question text dissolves. ACC2 now releases malonyl blocks that travel only a short way to the CPT-I door and hold it shut; a few of ACC1's blocks also drift there, but most of the blocks at the door come from ACC2. On 'building block', ACC1's blocks pulse as they enter the loop and a tag 'building block' appears under ACC1. On 'signal', the blocks at the door pulse and a tag 'signal' appears under ACC2.

scenes.tts: Follow a well-fed cell. Insulin and plentiful citrate push A C C on, and malonyl C O A rises. The synthase gets its extenders, and the C P T one gate closes. A cell that is building fat tends not to burn it.
scenes.caption: Follow a well-fed cell. Insulin and plentiful citrate push ACC on, and malonyl CoA rises. The synthase gets its extenders, and the CPT-I gate closes. A cell that is building fat tends not to burn it.
scenes.narration: Follow a well-fed cell. Insulin and plentiful citrate push ACC on, and malonyl CoA rises. The synthase gets its extenders, and the CPT-I gate closes. A cell that is building fat tends not to burn it.
scenes.visual: Label at top: 'fed state'. An insulin signal arrow from the frame edge and citrate tokens push the ACC levers to ON. A gauge labelled 'malonyl CoA' at the centre rises (schematic, no numbers). In step with the narration, the CRDR loop speeds up and palmitate bars roll off it, while the CPT-I door locks shut. On the last sentence, the palmitate bars stack neatly on the floor beside the loop instead of drifting toward the mitochondrion; the mitochondrion's swirl stays dim.

scenes.tts: So the answer to our question is one small molecule with two jobs. In the cytoplasm it is a brick for the chain. At the mitochondrion it is a lock on the door. So a cell tends not to build and burn at once.
scenes.caption: So the answer to our question is one small molecule with two jobs. In the cytoplasm it is a brick for the chain. At the mitochondrion it is a lock on the door. So a cell tends not to build and burn at once.
scenes.narration: So the answer to our question is one small molecule with two jobs. In the cytoplasm it is a brick for the chain. At the mitochondrion it is a lock on the door. So a cell tends not to build and burn at once.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the opening composition. One malonyl block is highlighted with its yellow badge. On 'a brick for the chain', a copy of it slots into the CRDR loop and the chain counter ticks up by two. On 'a lock on the door', a second copy settles into the closed CPT-I door. The stacked palmitate bars sit safely on the floor. The opening question 'What keeps new fat unburned?' briefly reappears and is answered by a short label 'malonyl CoA' that slides beneath it.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world: the CRDR loop circling slowly, the CPT-I door closed, the mitochondrion's swirl faint. Large white text, centred: 'The malonyl CoA that builds fat also shuts the gate to burning.'
